scenarioSubtitle: Designing an AI-enabled SME customer journey
description: Participants make AI leadership decisions across the customer journey and see how those choices affect customer economic value over time.

rounds.title: How should we use AI in SME acquisition emails?
rounds.prompt: The team wants to improve campaign performance for SME customers. How much AI personalization should be applied at the acquisition stage?

options.label: Hyper-personalize every email with agent-generated content for each SME
options.explanation: This increases relevance, but acquisition email is a relatively low-value touchpoint. The added orchestration and API cost reduce economic efficiency and create slight downstream drag.

options.label: Use AI to personalize selected content and high-value moments only
options.explanation: This creates a better balance between relevance and cost. It improves acquisition and carries a meaningful uplift into onboarding, activation, and beyond.

options.label: Keep generic rule-based campaign software
options.explanation: Lower relevance weakens conversion immediately and suppresses value creation across the entire customer journey.

rounds.title: How should the AI support onboarding?
rounds.prompt: The bank wants to streamline onboarding. Should it fully automate, selectively guide, or preserve traditional flows?

options.label: Fully automate onboarding with minimal explanation and no human escalation
options.explanation: Onboarding completes quickly, but opacity in a high-trust moment destroys confidence. The short-term onboarding gain reverses into a severe and lasting drop across activation, engagement, and retention.

options.label: Use guided AI onboarding with transparency and human support when needed
options.explanation: This reduces friction while preserving confidence and control. The strong onboarding experience carries visibly all the way through to loyalty — the highest-propagation decision in the simulation.

options.label: Keep mostly manual onboarding with static digital forms
options.explanation: Avoiding AI avoids risk, but leaves a fragmented experience in place. The drag shows clearly at onboarding and compounds across every downstream stage.

rounds.title: How proactive should the AI be in helping the customer get started?
rounds.prompt: Once onboarded, the SME customer needs help using the service. What role should AI play in activation?

options.label: Push aggressive next-best actions immediately across all users
options.explanation: Activation metrics improve in the short term, but overly aggressive prompts erode trust and create a noticeable reversal through engagement and retention.

options.label: Use AI to recommend contextual next steps based on behavior and needs
options.explanation: This creates strong activation momentum without overwhelming the customer. The improvement compounds clearly into engagement and loyalty.

options.label: Let customers figure it out themselves using menus and dashboards
options.explanation: Low guidance causes a visible activation slump and weakens engagement meaningfully. The experience never fully recovers its momentum.

rounds.title: How much autonomy should the AI have in ongoing support?
rounds.prompt: The bank is designing the day-to-day AI experience. How much autonomy should the AI agent have during engagement?

options.label: Let the AI act autonomously across most interactions and recommendations
options.explanation: Autonomy improves engagement metrics in the short term, but the trust erosion is severe. The reversal at retention and loyalty is among the most dramatic in the simulation — a clear autonomy trap.

options.label: Use AI for proactive guidance, with customer visibility and control over key actions
options.explanation: The strongest engagement design: useful, proactive, and aligned with customer agency. The uplift at engagement is large and carries powerfully into expansion, retention, and loyalty.

options.label: Keep AI passive and only surface information when explicitly requested
options.explanation: The experience remains static and underuses AI at the moment it would create the most value. Engagement, expansion, and retention all take a compounding hit.

rounds.title: How should AI shape growth offers and recommendations?
rounds.prompt: The SME is now an active customer. The bank wants to drive expansion through AI-enabled offers. What should it do?

options.label: Use generic AI-generated upsell offers across the customer base
options.explanation: Generic offers produce a visible expansion bump, but disconnected recommendations feel impersonal. The loyalty damage at the end of the journey is a clear consequence of trading relevance for scale.

options.label: Use contextual AI recommendations tied to business signals, behavior, and likely needs
options.explanation: This turns AI into a true growth partner. The expansion lift is the largest single-stage impact in the simulation, and it sustains strongly into retention and loyalty.

options.label: Avoid proactive expansion recommendations and wait for the customer to ask
options.explanation: Reactive expansion consistently misses the customer at the moment of readiness. The drag is visible at expansion and compounds into retention and loyalty.

rounds.title: How should the AI respond to emerging risk and churn signals?
rounds.prompt: The bank can see signals that some SME customers may struggle or disengage. How should AI respond?

options.label: Let AI intervene automatically without customer explanation or review
options.explanation: Automatic intervention recovers some retention, but opaque action in a sensitive moment seriously damages trust. The retention gain fully reverses into a loyalty loss — a clear autonomy-transparency trade-off.

options.label: Use AI to detect risk early and offer transparent, actionable support options
options.explanation: The highest-leverage decision in the simulation: early detection, relevant support, trust-preserving intervention. The impact on retention and loyalty is the most visible and consequential in the entire journey.

options.label: Wait until the customer raises a problem or shows clear churn behavior
options.explanation: Reactive handling means the intervention always arrives too late. The damage to retention and loyalty is immediate and clearly visible on the chart.
